geo_headlines: OIL DROPS ON IRAN DIPLOMACY. **January Brent $108.49 (-4.4%) and December WTI $99.53 (-4.4%), back below $100, after Iranian negotiators held a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets Iran's conditions (Reuters, AP).** OPEC+ agreed over the weekend to keep December quotas unchanged (dpa via Yahoo).

TRUMP LEANS TOWARD TALKS, FOR NOW. Netanyahu pressed Trump in a Saturday call to strike Iran right after Tuesday's midterms, but Trump wants to let negotiations play out for now while preparing for possible renewed combat (Axios). At an Iowa rally Sunday he said the US may at some point have to deliver a devastating blow (Mezha, RFE/RL).

FUTURES REBOUND. S&P 500 futures 7,652.75 (+0.5%) and Nasdaq 100 futures 28,767 (+0.8%) after Friday's tech rout. Europe is flat: STOXX 600 about unchanged, Alstom sharply lower on a forecast cut, and Fitch cut France's outlook (Reuters, Sharecast, Investing.com).
ASIA MIXED. Kospi +2.3%, Shanghai +1.2% and Hang Seng +0.6%; Nikkei -0.1% and TSMC -1.5%. China's official factory gauge slipped back into contraction in October (AP).

APPLE AND PALANTIR TONIGHT. Apple reports after the close, its first call under CEO John Ternus; analysts expect about $2.00 a share on about $113 billion in revenue, with early iPhone 18 demand in focus. Apple has overtaken Nvidia as the most valuable listed company (Reuters, Investing.com).

THIS WEEK. ISM manufacturing today 10:00 AM. Tuesday: midterm elections, JOLTS. Wednesday: ADP, ISM services. Friday: October payrolls 8:30 AM, consensus 55,000 (Dow Jones via JKN) to 65,000 (ThriveInMarkets) after September's 29,000. Reports cite possible US strikes as early as Wednesday.
client_frame_short: A calmer Monday morning. Oil is down more than 4% and back under $100 for US crude as Iran and Qatari mediators keep talking, and stock futures are bouncing after Friday's tech rout. **The catch is timing: Apple reports tonight, the midterms are tomorrow, Israel is reportedly pressing for strikes right after the vote, and the jobs report lands Friday, so this week can swing both ways.** For clients: one calm morning does not change the plan, and neither would one rough one; stay diversified and rebalance toward targets.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the short version is that the weekend brought more diplomacy than escalation, and markets are taking some relief from it.

What changed overnight: oil fell more than 4%, with Brent near $108 and US crude back under $100, after Iranian negotiators spent a third day with Qatari mediators on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets Iran's conditions. Axios reports President Trump wants to let talks play out for now, even as Israel presses for strikes right after Tuesday's vote; at a rally Trump also warned the US may at some point need to deliver a devastating blow. Stock futures are up about 0.5% for the S&P 500 and 0.8% for the Nasdaq 100. OPEC+ left output targets unchanged.

Where we stand: Friday the S&P 500 fell 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Intel and Amazon, leaving the S&P about 3% below its October 6 record close. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.94%, and futures markets still see about a 72% chance of a December rate hike.

The week ahead: Apple reports tonight, the first call under its new CEO; the midterms are tomorrow; AMD reports Tuesday; and the October jobs report is Friday, with economists expecting a modest 55,000 to 65,000 new jobs.

Why it matters: lower oil is the most direct relief valve for inflation and rate-hike fears. If talks hold, that helps bonds and stocks alike; if they break down after the vote, oil can reverse quickly. Diversified portfolios are built for either outcome.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and avoid election-week or Iran-headline trades in either direction. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Friday 4.94%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Friday 5.31%), or US strikes that keep Brent well above $105 (now $108.49, down from $113.43 Friday).
